sections.skill: Explain that fairness goals can conflict and require a decision

questions.prompt: What does "equal error rates" aim for?

choices.text: The same chance of being wrongly flagged in each group
Exactly the same number of people approved in each group

questions.correct_answer: The same chance of being wrongly flagged in each group
questions.intro: "Fair" can mean different things, and the meanings can CONFLICT. One goal: EQUAL ERROR RATES, so each group faces the same chance of being wrongly flagged. Another: EQUAL SELECTION RATES, so each group is approved at the same rate. Another: CALIBRATION, where a score of "70% likely" means the same thing for every group. Researchers have shown that, when groups differ in underlying rates, these goals usually cannot all be met at once. So choosing a fairness goal is a DECISION about values that people must make and explain, not a purely technical setting.

sections.skill: Compare fairness goals with splitting a pizza

questions.prompt: How many ideas of fair are in the example?

choices.text: One, because there is only ever one correct way to divide any pizza fairly

questions.intro: Splitting a pizza "fairly" among friends can mean different things. EQUAL slices for everyone? Bigger slices for those who are hungrier? Slices based on who paid more? Each is a reasonable idea of fair, and you cannot do all three at once if people differ in hunger and payment. The group has to decide which idea to use, and explain it. AI fairness goals work the same way.

questions.prompt: Can all three ideas be met at once when people differ?

choices.text: Yes, by cutting the pizza into a very large number of tiny slices for everyone

sections.title: Apply it

questions.prompt: What should a team disclose about its fairness choice?

choices.text: Nothing at all, because fairness choices are trade secrets that must never be shared
Which goal, why, who was consulted and the trade-offs

questions.correct_answer: Which goal, why, who was consulted and the trade-offs
questions.intro: Reasonable people disagree about which goal matters most in a given setting, and this course does not settle that. What can be expected is transparency: say which goal was chosen, why, who was consulted, and what trade-offs it creates. Laws may also set requirements in some areas, such as hiring and lending. Revisit the choice as evidence and circumstances change.
